question: to the Commission Pina Picierno (Renew), Nathalie Loiseau (Renew), Lucia Yar (Renew), Dainius Žalimas (Renew), Ľubica Karvašová (Renew), Elisabetta Gualmini (Renew), Dan Barna (Renew), Lukas Sieper (Renew), Malik Azmani (Renew), Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová (Renew), Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann (Renew) Subject:

On 24 March 2026, the Tbilisi Court sentenced Elene Khoshtaria, leader of the opposition party Droa, to 18 months’ imprisonment for defacing election posters of the ruling Georgian Dream party as an act of protest in solidarity with an activist who had been arrested for the same action. Amnesty International has described the conviction as politically motivated1. Khoshtaria’s legal team has reported a serious deterioration in her health condition, including severe joint pain, increasing difficulty in moving and an inability to write2. The European Parliament has already acknowledged this situation and the need for specialised medical care in its resolution3, however the Georgian authorities continue to ignore requests for an adequate treatment plan. In the light of the above, can the Commission clarify: 1.

Whether it intends to exert formal pressure on the Georgian authorities to ensure that Khoshtaria receives adequate specialised medical care, in accordance with Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights;

Whether it considers that the sentence imposed on Khoshtaria for a symbolic act of protest constitutes a violation of the right to freedom of expression as protected by the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights;

What concrete measures it intends to take to secure the release of Khoshtaria and other political prisoners, including within the framework of the EU-Georgia dialogue and the instruments provided for under the EU-Georgia Association Agreement.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.8.2026) The Commission and the European External Action Service (EEAS) have kept Georgia high on their agenda amid democratic backsliding and the deterioration of human rights. The Commission and the EEAS held frequent discussions with Member States in the Foreign Affairs Council. The EU consistently recalls that Georgia must respect, protect and fulfil human rights and fundamental freedoms under international law. In March 2026, the EU suspended visa-free travel for holders of Georgian diplomatic, service, official passports due to persistent breaches of the fundamental rights benchmarks of the EU-Georgia visa-free regime. A technical meeting with the authorities took place on 11 June 2026. Failure to address the 2024–2025 Visa Suspension Mechanism recommendations may lead to further measures. Efforts by the EEAS to resume the Human Rights Dialogue with Georgia have so far not materialised. The Commission condemns the repression of opposition leaders, journalists and civil society and expresses solidarity with all those arbitrarily detained, ill-treated or imprisoned, including Elene Khoshtaria. The Commission appreciates the European Parliament's efforts to keep Georgia’s human rights situation under scrutiny, including through the urgency debate on Ms Khoshtaria's case in March 2026. The EU expects the authorities to ensure adequate medical care in line with Article 3 European Convention on Human Rights and will continue to monitor and raise her case together with those of other arbitrarily detained persons.
